title: Question 11
stem: Positron emission tomography (PET) is used in medical imaging.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a medical tracer.

markscheme_points.text: substance containing radioactive nuclei introduced into body and absorbed by tissue / organ

hints: Hint 1: Recall the formal Cambridge definition regarding PET scanning. State clearly the physical conditions and quantities involved.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: A positron annihilates with an electron to produce two $\gamma$-ray photons.
parts.text: Show that the minimum energy of each $\gamma$-ray photon is $8.2 \times 10^{-14}\text{ J}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in PET scanning connecting them.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Pet scanning. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$E = m c^2 = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \times (3.00 \times 10^8)^2 = 8.2 \times 10^{-14}\text{ J}$
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the wavelength of each $\gamma$-ray photon.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in PET scanning connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Pet scanning. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$\lambda = hc / E = (6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.00 \times 10^8) / (8.20 \times 10^{-14})$; $\lambda = 2.43 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m}$
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
